name: HUD Fair Market Rents (FMR) API
measures: HUD's annual Fair Market Rent estimates by bedroom count (studio-4BR), used for Section 8/voucher payment standards — a standardized, government rent benchmark per county/metro area.
coverage: national (all US counties and metro FMR areas)
granularity: county-level FMR is published per HUD Metro FMR Area, not per county within a metro — all five NYC boroughs (each its own county) sit inside one 'New York, NY HUD Metro FMR Area' along with Putnam/Rockland/Westchester, so plain county-level FMR gives a single number across every NYC NTA, i.e. no intra-NYC signal. The usable product for this project is Small Area FMR (SAFMR), published at ZIP-code level for most large metros including NYC — that's the primary granularity to target, not an optional extra.
history_available: multiple past fiscal years available via the API (exact depth not confirmed in this pass — check huduser.gov/hudapi docs)
license: Governed by https://www.huduser.gov/portal/dataset/api-terms-of-service.html. A third-party mirror labels the FMR API 'Public Domain'; HUD's terms reportedly require a non-endorsement notice ('uses the HUD User Data API ... not endorsed or certified by HUD User') when the data is used in an app. No commercial-use block found, but read the official terms page before shipping.
recommendation: The project's rent-growth and rent-yield metrics (zori_cagr_3y, gross_rent_yield) currently lean on Zillow's ZORI, which has uneven metro coverage and isn't a government series. HUD FMR is free, no-trial, and nationally complete, but plain county-level FMR is useless as an NYC neighborhood signal (one value for all five boroughs via the shared metro FMR area) — the scoring in neighborhood.py compares NTAs against each other, so a flat metric adds nothing. Small Area FMR (ZIP-level) is the version actually worth implementing: it would give real intra-NYC variation and still generalizes nationally wherever SAFMRs are published. Recommend conditional on confirming SAFMR coverage for NYC ZIPs; downgrade to don't-recommend if it turns out not to be published for this metro.
open_questions: Confirm SAFMRs are actually published for NYC-metro ZIP codes (not just the big flat county/metro FMR) — this is the crux of whether this source is usable at all for neighborhood scoring.
